overview: Two continuous regions of the same organelle network, distinguished by the presence or absence of ribosomes and by function.
genZNote: Rough ER: protein factory with a bumpy roof. Smooth ER: the chill lipid lab next door.

aspects.label: Overview / Core Definition
aspects.valueA: ER studded with ribosomes on its cytoplasmic surface, specialized for synthesizing and processing proteins destined for secretion or membranes.
aspects.valueB: ER without ribosomes, specialized for lipid synthesis, detoxification, and calcium storage.

aspects.label: Ribosome Presence
aspects.valueA: Studded with ribosomes, giving it a "rough" appearance under the microscope.
aspects.valueB: Lacks ribosomes, giving it a smooth appearance.

aspects.label: Primary Function
aspects.valueA: Synthesis, folding, and initial modification (e.g. glycosylation) of secretory and membrane proteins.
aspects.valueB: Lipid and steroid synthesis, carbohydrate metabolism, and detoxification of drugs/toxins (notable in liver cells).

aspects.label: Relative Abundance by Cell Type
aspects.valueA: Abundant in cells that secrete large amounts of protein (e.g. pancreatic acinar cells, plasma cells).
aspects.valueB: Abundant in cells with high lipid/steroid synthesis or detoxification needs (e.g. liver hepatocytes, steroid-producing gonadal cells).

aspects.label: Calcium Storage
aspects.valueA: Some capacity, but this is a more prominent smooth ER role.
aspects.valueB: Major site of calcium ion storage and release, especially in muscle cells (sarcoplasmic reticulum).
